critical_bugs: subprocess.run calls lack a timeout parameter, which can cause the entire pipeline to hang indefinitely if a stage script deadlocks or waits for input.
Pipeline execution continues regardless of stage failures; run_stage returns a boolean success flag that is never checked, risking downstream stages processing incomplete or corrupted data.
Interactive input() calls will raise unhandled EOFError when stdin is closed or piped, causing abrupt crashes in automated/CI environments.
warnings: Modifying sys.path at runtime can cause import shadowing and conflicts with standard Python packaging practices.
Subprocess stdout and stderr are not captured or logged, making it difficult to diagnose why a stage failed.
Fallback calibration path uses os.path.dirname(root), which may resolve to an unexpected parent directory depending on how the project is mounted or invoked.
recommendations: Add timeout=300 (or appropriate duration) to all subprocess.run calls and handle subprocess.TimeoutExpired explicitly.
Replace interactive input() prompts with argparse CLI arguments to enable non-interactive execution, scheduling, and CI/CD integration.
Implement the logging module instead of print(), and capture subprocess output using capture_output=True, text=True for audit trails.
Add conditional checks after run_stage calls to halt or gracefully skip downstream stages if critical upstream steps fail.
Remove sys.path.insert(0, THIS_DIR); refactor into a proper Python package structure or use PYTHONPATH/environment variables.

critical_bugs: Path traversal vulnerability via symlink attack in session directory handling
warnings: Pipeline continues processing after stage failure (no early termination)
Calibration file resolution may fail silently if both paths are invalid
recommendations: Add path validation to ensure session_path is within project root before processing
Implement immediate pipeline termination on any stage failure
Verify calibration file existence after resolution and exit with clear error message
